requested_parts: Difference among Damage, Destroy, Remove, Replace for survival and Fear
Combining Damage from separate normal Powers
answers.answer: Damage from separate normal Powers can accumulate within a turn, and normal Spirit Damage is to Invaders unless specified; it does not harm Dahan. Destroy returns pieces regardless of Health and yields Town 1 Fear/City 2 Fear; Remove returns pieces without destruction Fear; Replace retains marked Damage, and the replacement itself yields no Fear unless that retained Damage destroys it. Damage can combine to destroy a piece.

evidence.text: “Damage” means **Damage to Invaders** unless explicitly stated otherwise. Normal Spirit Damage does not harm Dahan or the land. Distribute Damage among Invaders in the target land however you wish; Explorers need not be hit first. Damage from separate normal Powers and counterattacks can accumulate within a turn. A piece is destroyed immediately when its marked Damage reaches/exceeds its Health. Reduced Health can also destroy a previously damaged piece; Damage does not itself reduce Health. Marked Damage does not reduce the Health counted by a Health-worth removal allowance. If a damaged piece moves out of a Health bonus or into a Health penalty and is thereby destroyed, destruction occurs in its destination land, never in an in-between location. [FAQ if-an-invader-with-health-bonus-and-damage-is-moved-where-is-it-destroyed]

**Destroy** returns pieces to supply regardless of Health when directly instructed. Every destroyed Town generates **1 Fear** and every destroyed City **2 Fear**, in addition to explicit Fear from the effect. Explorers generate none automatically. **Remove** returns the specified pieces without requiring Damage to reach their Health and without destruction Fear. Within the effect's count and piece-type restrictions, its decision-maker may choose any eligible pieces; there is no Explorer-first priority unless stated. **Replace** removes a piece and adds another, retaining its marked Damage: the replacement itself produces no Fear, but if the retained Damage destroys the new piece, destruction Fear applies normally. For simultaneous replacements, select all pieces before replacing any: the same original City cannot become a Town and then an Explorer within that one simultaneous instruction. Separate completed instructions or actions may replace the resulting piece again (e.g., successive players resolving **Trade Suffers** at Terror III).

requested_parts: Whether illegally placed Invader can remain after action tree
Cleanup destination and whether relocation triggers movement effects
answers.answer: No. After the primary action and triggers finish, Push survivors to non-Ocean land within that action if possible. After the action tree, remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land; cleanup is not movement and triggers nothing.

evidence.text: - **Drowning:** Ocean's rule Drowns Invaders/Dahan **after** they move into the Ocean on a board with Ocean's Presence; Ocean need not have a disk in the Ocean itself. Drown destroys: Town/City Fear happens immediately, and drowned Invaders go on Ocean's panel. At any time, trade stored Invaders: **X printed Health worth of drowned Invaders for 1 Energy**, X = number of Spirits; ignore Health modifiers and make change. They need not be exchanged when Drowned; Ocean may exchange them between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards. Dahan drowning gives no Energy. For these rules, **humans** means all Invaders (Explorers, Towns and Cities) and Dahan. Ordinary destruction, including thematically watery Powers, is not Drowning unless specified. If Ocean loses all Presence on that board mid-action, Ocean In Play lasts through the action tree; afterward non-human pieces left there remain physically but out of play until it returns. Humans cannot stay there between action trees: if Drowning fails, Push survivors to non-Ocean lands within that action. This is an actual Push and can trigger applicable movement effects, unlike later cleanup. Failed Drowning yields no Energy. **After the primary action and all triggered actions finish**, remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land. This post-action-tree correction uses the cleanup procedure below. Cleanup is not an action, move, removal or destruction and triggers nothing, and occurs before the outcome check. requested_parts: Whether losing Earth Sacred Site retroactively removes Defend from simultaneous Dahan damage
answers.answer: No. Losing Earth's defending Sacred Site to Blight does not retroactively remove its Defend from the simultaneous Damage to Dahan during that Ravage.

evidence.text: Dahan do not shield the land; Damage to them is not subtracted from land Damage. **After Invader damage is fully resolved**, surviving Dahan each deal **2 Damage** to Invaders in that land, allocated by the players. A damaged surviving Dahan still deals 2. Surviving Dahan counterattack even when Invader Damage was reduced to zero by Defend, but not when the entire Ravage was skipped. Presence never counterattacks. If a Power changes Dahan Ravage Damage timing, that replaces their usual counterattack timing; each Dahan deals Ravage Damage only once. **Words of Warning** makes Dahan and Invader Ravage Damage simultaneous, so Dahan killed in that exchange still deal their Damage, with no second later counterattack. Losing Earth's defending Sacred Site to the resulting Blight does not retroactively remove its Defend from the simultaneous Damage to Dahan in that Ravage. [FAQ number-of-counterattacks-when-dahan-counterattack-early; .bu6oc8y]
